Updates `astral-sh/setup-uv` from 3.2.0 to 4.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v4.2.0 🌈 Resolve latest version instead of downloading latest release

Changes

We got a frist contribution from @​pollenjp!

Thanks to this we are now resolving the latest version and try to find it in the local cache instead of always downloading the latest release from the uv repository. This new approach is not only more efficient, it also fixes a latent bug in the self-hosted runners tools cache and makes the code more maintainable.

Thank you @​pollenjp!

🚀 Enhancements

  • Resolve latest version instead of downloading latest release @​pollenjp (#178)

🧰 Maintenance

  • Add test for python-version @​eifinger (#177)

v4.1.0 🌈 Set UV_PYTHON for your workflow

Changes

You can now use the input python-version to set the environment variable UV_PYTHON for the rest of your workflow. This will override any python version specifications in pyproject.toml and .python-version

- name: Install the latest version of uv and set the python version to 3.12
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
  with:
    python-version: "3.12"

You can combine this with a matrix to test multiple python versions:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install the latest version of uv and set the python version
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - name: Test with python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        run: uv run --frozen pytest

+{% set name = "mpfun90" %}

+  version: {{ version }}

+
+build:
+  skip: true  # [win]
+  number: 0
+  run_exports:

I'm not asking for reasons unrelated to this issue and mostly just out of pure curiosity, but can you tell me a bit about how the HEP theory/phenomenology community uses these? Is Gentoo a common distro that people have standardized around? I don't have experience with [EasyBuild](https://docs.easybuild.io/) and I guess EESSI is https://github.com/EESSI(?). It seems that both are focused on HPCs specifically. I assume this isn't about compiler optimisation but about automating HPC specific builds as all HPCs have their own oddities? 

> Maybe one could think of some sort of organization that coordinates/communicates between all the efforts

Maybe. I think it would help to understand why each exists in the first place.

The reason that I'm drawn to using conda-forge for packaging and distribution is that it offers multi-platform support and so you don't have to resolve packaging for each Linux distribution. I appreciate that Nix addresses this too, but there doesn't seem to be widespread use of Nix anywhere in HEP at the moment (the repo you link to is even archived). I also realistically don't know enough about the subtleties of HPC computing to be able to offer much insight here, as most of my "HPC" work is on GPUs and I tend to work on HTC systems more. +{% set name = "mpfun90" %}
+{% set version = "2024-12-05" | replace('-', '.') %}
+
+package:
+  name: {{ name }}
+  version: {{ version }}
+
+source:
+  # need to match the GitHub version tag but only want one variable
+  url: https://github.com/APN-Pucky/mpfun90/archive/{{ version | replace('.', '-') }}.tar.gz
+  sha256: a273027f373eaa23743503612de4ca448628b5c1521510c21d5da3a5cfde79f5
+
+build:
+  skip: true  # [win]
+  number: 0
+  run_exports:
+    # MPFUN90 is archival software and the ABI should be static
+    - {{ pin_subpackage('mpfun90', max_pin='x') }}
+  ignore_run_exports_from:
+    - sed  # [not linux]
+  script:
+    # FIXME: https://github.com/APN-Pucky/mpfun90/commit/d00bfe06b8f69329464906817f7f8b795bed5388
+    - sed -i 's/ -Wl,--as-needed -Wl,-soname,libmpfun90.so / /g' Makefile  # [not linux]
+
+    - sed -i "s/libmpfun90.so/libmpfun90${SHLIB_EXT}/g" Makefile  # [not linux]
+    - export LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -lgfortran"  # [not linux]
+    - make dynamic FC="$FC" FFLAGS="$FFLAGS"
+    - mv libmpfun90${SHLIB_EXT} $PREFIX/lib/
+    - mkdir -p $PREFIX/include/mpfun90
+    - mv *.mod $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/
+    - make clean
+
+requirements:
+  build:
+    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+    - {{ compiler('fortran') }}
+    - make
+    - sed  # [not linux]
+
+test:
+  commands:
+    - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libmpfun90${SHLIB_EXT}
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfuna.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunb.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunc.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfund.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfune.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunf.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfung.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunh.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfuni.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunj.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpdefmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpintmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mprealmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpcmpmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpgenmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpfunsubmod.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpmodule.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpmodulem.mod
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/mpfun90/mpmodulex.mod
+
+about:
+  home: https://github.com/APN-Pucky/mpfun90
+  summary: 'MPFUN90: A multiple precision floating point computation package'

+    It is based on the work described in
+    David H. Bailey, "_A Fortran 90-based multiprecision system_,"

+source:
+  url: https://github.com/gstagnit/{{ name }}/archive/v{{ version }}.tar.gz

+  folder: source
+  patches:

+
+build:
+  skip: true  # [win]
+  number: 0
+  run_exports:
+    - {{ pin_subpackage('emela', max_pin='x.x') }}
+  script:
+    - cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$PREFIX -DWITH_LHAPDF=ON -S source -B build
+    - cmake -LH build
+    - cmake --build build --clean-first --parallel="${CPU_COUNT}"
+    - cmake --install build
+
+requirements:
+  build:
+    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+    - {{ compiler('fortran') }}
+    - cmake
+    - make
+  host:

+    - lhapdf
+  run:
+    - lhapdf
+
+test:
+  source_files:
+    - source/example
+  requires:
+    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+    - cmake
+    - make
+    - curl
+    - tar
+  commands:
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/version.h
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/bspdf.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/analytics.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/specialfunctions.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/version.h.in
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/constants.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/eMELA.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/grid.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/ilc500.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/include/eMELA/numerics.hh
+    - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libeMELA${SHLIB_EXT}
+    - test -f $PREFIX/bin/eMELA-config
+
+    - eMELA-config --help
+    - eMELA-config --prefix
+    - eMELA-config --incdir
+    - eMELA-config --libdir
+    - eMELA-config --data
+    - eMELA-config --cppflags
+    - eMELA-config --cxxflags
+    - eMELA-config --ldflags
+
+    - cd source/example
+    - $CXX CreateGrid.cc -o CreateGrid $CXXFLAGS $LDFLAGS $(eMELA-config --ldflags)
+    # Skip as extremely slow with 50000 grid points
+    # - ./CreateGrid NLL DELTA MSBAR
+    - test -f ./CreateGrid
+    - $CXX GetPdf.cc -o GetPdf $CXXFLAGS $LDFLAGS $(eMELA-config --ldflags)
+    - ./GetPdf
+

> Regardless, `libooptools.a` won't actually be needed at runtime.

I think my lack of C++ skill is showing here, but if a library is required for an interface to work at execution time, isn't that the same as a runtime requirement?

> This means that once the binary (e.g., `libninja` or `simple_test`) is built, `ooptools` is no longer needed at runtime because its code has already been included in the final binary.

doesn't seem correct just given the execution failure.

```diff

@@ -53,6 +52,7 @@ test:

     - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libninja${SHLIB_EXT}

@@ -110,6 +110,9 @@ test:
     - make clean
     - echo -e "\n# simple_test by hand"
```

+{% set name = "ninja" %}
+{% set version = "1.2.0" %}
+
+package:
+  name: {{ name }}-hep-ph
+  version: {{ version }}
+
+source:
+  url: https://github.com/peraro/ninja/archive/v{{ version }}.tar.gz
+  sha256: b9709aada408286b6533ac7427bab9d1364d449a9c11098c324ea0875fe9a9e1
+  patches:
+    - posix-compliant-shell.patch
+    - update-version-number-to-v1.2.0.patch
+
+build:
+  # libquadmath is required, so macOS is not supported
+  skip: true  # [not linux]
+  number: 0
+  run_exports:
+    - {{ pin_subpackage('ninja-hep-ph', max_pin='x.x') }}
+
+requirements:
+  build:
+    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+    - {{ compiler('fortran') }}
+    - automake  # includes autoconf
+    - libtool
+    - make
+    - pkg-config
+    - gnuconfig
+    - oneloop  # [build_platform != target_platform]
+    - looptools-static  # [build_platform != target_platform]
+  host:
+    - oneloop
+    - looptools-static

Similarly, if inspected on https://prefix.dev/channels/conda-forge/packages/pythia8 there seems to be no reported difference in the dependencies.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67e0f77-3fa0-444f-8331-3fa7937308e4)

This does not happen with other cross-compiled packages like LHAPDF: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/lhapdf/files?version=6.5.4

@chrisburr any ideas on why? `pythia8` is a large package so I don't want to be taking up GB of storage on conda-forge that is never going to get used.

```yaml
requirements:
  build:
    - python                                 # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - cross-python_{{ target_platform }}     # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - x86_64-microarch-level {{ microarch_level }}  # [unix and x86_64]
    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
```

and not

```yaml
requirements:
  build:
    - python                                 # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - cross-python_{{ target_platform }}     # [build_platform != target_platform]
    - x86_64-microarch-level {{ microarch_level }}  # [unix and x86_64 and (build_platform == target_platform)]
    - {{ stdlib('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('c') }}
    - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
```

Comment:

As described in https://github.com/conda-forge/pythia8-feedstock/issues/53, I've noticed that for feedstocks with microarch-level enabled _and_ cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) that the cross-compile builds are getting built twice for no clear reason.

> I've noticed that the cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) are getting built twice for reasons I don't understand. This can be seen on https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/pythia8/files if you search for "`linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312`" then both `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312h9243d74_0.conda` and `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312hd40b618_0.conda` are found. Similarly, if inspected on https://prefix.dev/channels/conda-forge/packages/pythia8 there seems to be no reported difference in the dependencies.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67e0f77-3fa0-444f-8331-3fa7937308e4)
> 
> This does not happen with other cross-compiled packages like LHAPDF: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/lhapdf/files?version=6.5.4

Can anyone advise as to what that might be?

Example feedstocks:
* [conda-forge/pythia8-feedstock](https://github.com/conda-forge/pythia8-feedstock/blob/825e5cae758bf6895668827ab86e594cad130dbe/recipe/meta.yaml)

Comment:

As described in https://github.com/conda-forge/pythia8-feedstock/issues/53, I've noticed that for feedstocks with microarch-level enabled _and_ cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) that the cross-compile builds are getting built twice for no clear reason.

> I've noticed that the cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) are getting built twice for reasons I don't understand. This can be seen on https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/pythia8/files if you search for "`linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312`" then both `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312h9243d74_0.conda` and `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312hd40b618_0.conda` are found. Similarly, if inspected on https://prefix.dev/channels/conda-forge/packages/pythia8 there seems to be no reported difference in the dependencies.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67e0f77-3fa0-444f-8331-3fa7937308e4)
> 
> This does not happen with other cross-compiled packages like LHAPDF: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/lhapdf/files?version=6.5.4

Can anyone advise as to what that might be?

As described in https://github.com/conda-forge/pythia8-feedstock/issues/53, I've noticed that for feedstocks with microarch-level enabled _and_ cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) that the cross-compile builds are getting built twice for no clear reason.

> I've noticed that the cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) are getting built twice for reasons I don't understand. This can be seen on https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/pythia8/files if you search for "`linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312`" then both `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312h9243d74_0.conda` and `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312hd40b618_0.conda` are found. > 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67e0f77-3fa0-444f-8331-3fa7937308e4)
> 
> This does not happen with other cross-compiled packages like LHAPDF: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/lhapdf/files?version=6.5.4

Can anyone advise as to what that might be?

### Issue

I've noticed that the cross-compile builds (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-ppc64le`, and `osx-arm64`) are getting built twice for reasons I don't understand. This can be seen on https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/pythia8/files if you search for "`linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312`" then both `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312h9243d74_0.conda` and `linux-aarch64/pythia8-8.312-py312hd40b618_0.conda` are found. Similarly, if inspected on https://prefix.dev/channels/conda-forge/packages/pythia8 there seems to be no reported difference in the dependencies.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f67e0f77-3fa0-444f-8331-3fa7937308e4)

This does not happen with other cross-compiled packages like LHAPDF: https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/lhapdf/files?version=6.5.4

@chrisburr any ideas on why? `pythia8` is a large package so I don't want to be taking up GB of storage on conda-forge that is never going to get used.

+{% set name = "fastjet-contrib" %}
+{% set version = "1.056" %}
+
+package:
+  name: {{ name }}
+  version: {{ version }}
+
+source:
+  url: https://fastjet.hepforge.org/contrib/downloads/fjcontrib-{{ version }}.tar.gz
+  sha256: fc31544424dece0d0676ea2433ad1e96fd9db82920bc7a7ef6294ce94e659d6e
+
+build:
+  number: 0
+
+outputs:
+  - name: {{ name }}
+
+    build:
+      skip: true  # [win]
+      run_exports:
+        - {{ pin_subpackage('fastjet-contrib', max_pin='x.x') }}
+      script:
+        # Get an updated config.sub and config.guess
+        - cp $BUILD_PREFIX/share/gnuconfig/config.* .
+        - ./configure --help
+        - ./configure --list
+        - ./configure --fastjet-config=$(command -v fastjet-config) --prefix=$PREFIX CXX=$CXX
+        - make --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make fragile-shared --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make check --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"  # [build_platform == target_platform]
+        - make install
+        - make fragile-shared-install
+        - make clean

+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libConstituentSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libEnergyCorrelator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libFlavorCone.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libGenericSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetCleanser.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetFFMoments.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetsWithoutJets.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libLundPlane.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libNsubjettiness.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libQCDAwarePlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libRecursiveTools.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libScJet.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSignalFreeBackgroundEstimator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSoftKiller.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSubjetCounting.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libValenciaPlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libVariableR.a
+
+    requirements:
+      build:
+        - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - automake
+        - libtool
+        - make
+        - pkg-config
+        - gnuconfig
+        - fastjet-cxx  # [build_platform != target_platform]
+      host:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+      run:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+
+    test:
+      requires:
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - curl
+        - tar
+        - grep
+        - sed

+{% set version = "1.056" %}
+
+package:
+  # Have top level name be unique from any outputs
+  # c.f. https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-forge.github.io/blob/abfc33db28c35e9a8f6b719d0021768f0d5d06be/docs/maintainer/knowledge_base.md?plain=1#L1749
+  name: {{ name }}-split
+  version: {{ version }}
+
+source:
+  url: https://fastjet.hepforge.org/contrib/downloads/fjcontrib-{{ version }}.tar.gz
+  sha256: fc31544424dece0d0676ea2433ad1e96fd9db82920bc7a7ef6294ce94e659d6e
+
+build:
+  number: 0
+
+outputs:
+  - name: {{ name }}
+
+    build:
+      skip: true  # [win]
+      run_exports:
+        - {{ pin_subpackage('fastjet-contrib', max_pin='x.x') }}
+      script:
+        # Get an updated config.sub and config.guess
+        - cp $BUILD_PREFIX/share/gnuconfig/config.* .
+        - ./configure --help
+        - ./configure --list
+        - ./configure --fastjet-config=$(command -v fastjet-config) --prefix=$PREFIX CXX=$CXX
+        - make --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make fragile-shared --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make check --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"  # [build_platform == target_platform]
+        - make install
+        - make fragile-shared-install
+        # Remove the static libraries that got installed
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libCentauro.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libClusteringVetoPlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libConstituentSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libEnergyCorrelator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libFlavorCone.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libGenericSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetCleanser.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetFFMoments.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetsWithoutJets.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libLundPlane.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libNsubjettiness.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libQCDAwarePlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libRecursiveTools.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libScJet.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSignalFreeBackgroundEstimator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSoftKiller.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSubjetCounting.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libValenciaPlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libVariableR.a
+
+    requirements:
+      build:
+        - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - automake
+        - libtool
+        - make
+        - pkg-config
+        - gnuconfig
+        - fastjet-cxx  # [build_platform != target_platform]
+      host:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+      run:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+
+    test:
+      requires:
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - curl
+        - tar
+        - grep
+        - sed
+      script: run_test_shared.sh
+

+{% set name = "fastjet-contrib" %}
+{% set version = "1.056" %}
+
+package:
+  # Have top level name be unique from any outputs
+  # c.f. https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-forge.github.io/blob/abfc33db28c35e9a8f6b719d0021768f0d5d06be/docs/maintainer/knowledge_base.md?plain=1#L1749
+  name: {{ name }}-split
+  version: {{ version }}
+
+source:
+  url: https://fastjet.hepforge.org/contrib/downloads/fjcontrib-{{ version }}.tar.gz
+  sha256: fc31544424dece0d0676ea2433ad1e96fd9db82920bc7a7ef6294ce94e659d6e
+
+build:
+  number: 0
+
+outputs:
+  - name: {{ name }}
+
+    build:
+      skip: true  # [win]
+      run_exports:
+        - {{ pin_subpackage('fastjet-contrib', max_pin='x.x') }}
+      script:
+        # Get an updated config.sub and config.guess
+        - cp $BUILD_PREFIX/share/gnuconfig/config.* .
+        - ./configure --help
+        - ./configure --list
+        - ./configure --fastjet-config=$(command -v fastjet-config) --prefix=$PREFIX CXX=$CXX
+        - make --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make fragile-shared --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"
+        - make check --jobs="${CPU_COUNT}"  # [build_platform == target_platform]
+        - make install
+        - make fragile-shared-install
+        # Remove the static libraries that got installed
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libCentauro.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libClusteringVetoPlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libConstituentSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libEnergyCorrelator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libFlavorCone.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libGenericSubtractor.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetCleanser.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetFFMoments.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libJetsWithoutJets.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libLundPlane.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libNsubjettiness.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libQCDAwarePlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libRecursiveTools.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libScJet.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSignalFreeBackgroundEstimator.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSoftKiller.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libSubjetCounting.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libValenciaPlugin.a
+        - rm $PREFIX/lib/libVariableR.a
+
+    requirements:
+      build:
+        - {{ stdlib('c') }}
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - automake
+        - libtool
+        - make
+        - pkg-config
+        - gnuconfig
+        - fastjet-cxx  # [build_platform != target_platform]
+      host:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+      run:
+        - fastjet-cxx
+
+    test:
+      requires:
+        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
+        - curl
+        - tar
+        - grep
+        - sed
+      script: run_test_shared.sh
+

From the feedstock it seems that microarch level 2 is intended and supported:

https://github.com/conda-forge/microarch-level-feedstock/blob/343bcd72c1897c63ed102dff3b45a483f828f18d/recipe/gen.py#L8-L11

However, it is not shown in the [conda-forge maintainer docs Knowledge Base example](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/knowledge_base/#microarch):

`recipe/conda_build_config.yaml`
```yaml
microarch_level:
  - 1
  - 3  # [unix and x86_64]
  - 4  # [unix and x86_64]
```

`recipe/meta.yaml`
```yaml
# ...
{% set build = 0 %}

build:
  number: {{ build }}          # [not (unix and x86_64)]
  number: {{ build + 100 }}    # [unix and x86_64 and microarch_level == 1]
  number: {{ build + 300 }}    # [unix and x86_64 and microarch_level == 3]
  number: {{ build + 400 }}    # [unix and x86_64 and microarch_level == 4]

requirements:
  build:
    - x86_64-microarch-level {{ microarch_level }}  # [unix and x86_64]
    - {{ compiler('c') }}
    # ...
# ...
```

Is there a reason for this? Comment:

As I'm fairly certain the NumPy maintainers are aware of, [conda-forge supports microarch-level builds for x86 archs](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/knowledge_base/#microarch). As NumPy currently doesn't have this enabled I'm going to assume that is for a reason, but to double check and use this as a piece of information for the rest of the community, is that because NumPy already has optimizations that don't require SIMD optimizations to be turned on? Is adding the microarch-level builds going to be too many packages per build for limited utility, and the NumPy team doesn't want to use lots of storage? Are the additional builds enough of a nuisance that this level of maintainer overhead not worthwhile? Have the maintainers not had the opportunity to properly do comparisons on if the level-3 SIMD optimizations are worth it? Something else?

Again, this is asking out of curiosity and to better inform other project decisions, not to insinuate that the NumPy team should be doing something more than everything you already Awesome. This is what I assumed, but I wanted to be sure.
